description: A call that resolves to nothing is a COMPILATION error: 'Unknown function NAME.' - the name upper-cased however it was written, a full stop at the end, and no position. A QUALIFIED name gets a different sentence, 'Unknown user-defined function SCHEMA.NAME.' Live-verified. The 'SQL compilation error:' prefix is load-bearing beyond its wording: it is what marks the error compile-time, which is how a CREATE VIEW over an unknown function comes to be refused at all, and why an EMPTY table is refused identically - the name is resolved while the statement is planned rather than while rows are produced. The refusal does not outrank everything, and the order is measured: an invalid IDENTIFIER wins over it wherever each of them stands, and a syntax error wins over both. CUBE and ROLLUP are ordinary unknown names when nested inside another super-group. Measured and deliberately NOT asserted: live ACCUMULATES the names when a statement has more than one, pluralising the noun and listing one entry per OCCURRENCE - SELECT zzzfn(1), aaafn(2) is 'Unknown functions ZZZFN, AAAFN.' where Frostlake names the first only; inside the super-groups the counts follow Snowflake's grouping-set EXPANSION, so CUBE (a, ROLLUP (b)) lists ROLLUP twice and CUBE (ROLLUP (a), ROLLUP (b)) lists it four times. Converted 1:1 from functions/UnknownFunctionRefusalTest (now retired); the class's setupTest created uf_t with one row so the expression was actually evaluated, which each converted test recreates.
